display_title: Validating an NLP Coding-Assist Model for KC-135 Maintenance Records
one_liner: A fine-tuned ModernBERT-large model that suggests the Work Unit Code for a KC-135 maintenance record. It was checked by re-measuring what the app actually served, which exposed a silent 14-point accuracy defect in production.
problem: Maintainers hand-assign one of roughly 1,300 Work Unit Codes to every KC-135 maintenance record. Miscoded records reduce the quality of reliability, sustainment and readiness analysis built on that data.
approach: Records from two extracts (2019-2026) were merged and deduplicated. Discrepancy and corrective-action text feeds a ModernBERT-large classifier over 1,251 codes, trained with class-weighted cross-entropy and hierarchical system/subsystem auxiliary losses. The served model was then evaluated on held-out records, with accuracy reported separately from label coverage, calibration by confidence band, and errors broken down by the WUC hierarchy.
decision_relevance: Supports the WUC coding decision on completed maintenance records. The top-3 suggestions plus a confidence band send low-confidence records to QC review. The confusion pairs found (for example, codes used interchangeably across bases) are direct feedback to data owners on inconsistent coding that distorts downstream analysis.

headline_results.claim: Top-1 accuracy 0.903 (95% CI 0.899-0.908) and top-3 0.978 on the 15,636-record held-out test split, scored against QC labels
headline_results.evidence: training/batch_predict.py on data_splits/test.parquet after the pooling fix; recorded in CLAUDE.md and GLIDEPATH.md. The CI is computed by the auditor from recorded n.

headline_results.claim: 98.3% of predictions fall in the correct aircraft system; 62.8% of errors are same-subsystem near misses
headline_results.evidence: training/error_analysis.py; counts (1,330 errors = 835/226/269 of 15,876) recorded in CLAUDE.md, arithmetic consistent

headline_results.claim: Label coverage 93.2% of records; end-to-end top-1 0.854 including records whose code is outside the model's label space
headline_results.evidence: training/batch_predict.py --exclude-seen; 15,876 of 17,041 records answerable; recorded in CLAUDE.md

headline_results.claim: Predictions shown at 70% confidence or higher (93% of answerable records) are correct 94.6% of the time (n=14,795)
headline_results.evidence: training/batch_predict.py calibration-by-band output recorded in CLAUDE.md; band counts sum to 15,876

headline_results.claim: Re-measuring the serving path found a silent train/serve pooling mismatch that had cut production top-1 accuracy from 0.897 to 0.756 for three months
headline_results.evidence: training/check_pooling.py; fix and guard in training/train_hierarchical.py (classifier_pooling='cls'); documented in CLAUDE.md

headline_results.claim: Flat and hierarchical variants are statistically indistinguishable (38 vs 29 wins on 67 one-sided disagreements, sign test p = 0.33)
headline_results.evidence: training/compare_models.py on 2,000 seeded test rows, recorded in CLAUDE.md; p-value recomputed by auditor

limitations: Accuracy is scored against QC-pipeline labels from the same process that produced the training labels. It has not been checked by a KC-135 subject-matter expert (a 25-case adjudication is pending), and the direction of any label-noise bias is unknown.

The split is random by record with exact-text deduplication only. It has no temporal holdout and no grouping by job control number, so near-duplicate leakage may inflate accuracy, and performance on future records is untested.
Built for post-fix coding: inputs include the corrective action. It is not a pre-repair predictor.
6.8% of records carry codes excluded from the label space (fewer than 5 training examples), so the model cannot predict them.
Single training seed; no run-to-run variance reported.
Training data and model weights are CUI and are not public; results cannot be reproduced externally.
The LLM-written profile narrative (Tab 3) can state details that are not in the data.
blockers_before_featuring: The README headlines training-time 0.903/0.772 and argues the hierarchical model is 'significantly better calibrated' from a 47% lower test loss. That loss is a 0.5-weighted composite and not comparable to the flat model's cross-entropy (CONTRADICTED; CLAUDE.md retracts it). Rewrite the README.
The README claims a '76%' confidence corresponds to about 76% empirical accuracy. No reliability analysis supports this (UNVERIFIED). Remove it.

Held-out 0.9162 top-1 / 0.9797 top-3 (in CLAUDE.md and the user guide) disagrees with the test-split 0.9032; the 95% CIs do not overlap and the gap is unexplained. It is likely caused by frequency weighting and by dropping label-ambiguous texts in the anti-join. Reconcile before displaying it.
'0.9162 is a floor' and 'if labels contain errors, true accuracy is higher' are logically unsupported (CONTRADICTED); remove them from all docs.
The user guide says '93.2% of codes in current use'; the figure is 93.2% of records (CONTRADICTED); fix the wording.
No baseline. Add at least the maintainer-typed WUC vs QC Corrected WUC agreement, plus a TF-IDF+LR or majority-class baseline.
No confidence intervals, seed variance, or committed evidence artifact (metrics JSON or a counts-only log) for any headline number.
Unverified README claims: per-run wall times (~57-60 min) and 'expected ~0.55-0.65 macro F1' for the discrepancy-only variant.
Unpinned requirements.txt, no synthetic data sample, and a README quick start that points at the stale FinalData.csv.
The README has stale paths (training scripts listed at root, FinalData.csv in the diagram, deleted jonday/wuc-model), no LICENSE file, and says 'Internal - not yet licensed' on a public repo.
